sections.heading: 1. Hook — The Real-World Challenge
sections.rationale: Fatu's stall story kept and shortened from 272 to about 70 words; 'make a killing' and the career framing removed.

sections.heading: 2. Learning Objectives
sections.rationale: Three objectives, one of them story writing that the lesson never teaches, replaced by two assessable reading objectives. Story writing moves to the next lesson and the optional extension.

sections.heading: 3. Prior Knowledge Activation
sections.rationale: The salty-food example is reused as a diagnostic item; answers were shown to learners and are now feedback after a choice.

sections.heading: 4. Core Concept — Concrete Foundation
sections.rationale: The flood example and the definitions are reused. Dropped the unsupported claim that cassava is planted 'only during dry seasons to avoid spoilage'. Reviewer to confirm.

sections.heading: 5. Core Concept — The Rule and Why It Works
sections.rationale: The rule that a cause 'will always lead to some effect' overgeneralizes; replaced by the 'always is too strong' check.

sections.heading: 6. Key Vocabulary
sections.rationale: Cause and effect definitions and the flooded-street example reused, condensed into key points.

sections.heading: 7. Worked Example 1
sections.rationale: The flood and cassava-price chain is kept as a short reading text. The invented figures (LD 200 to LD 400, 10 to 2 tons) are dropped because they were not labelled as invented.

sections.heading: 8. Worked Example 2 — Alternative Method
sections.rationale: The 'start from the effect' method is kept and applied to a text with no signal word.

sections.heading: 9. Error Analysis
sections.rationale: Error 3 (overgeneralization) is reused. Error 1's correction is wrong: more buyers can raise prices, so it was removed. Reviewer to confirm.

sections.heading: 10. Guided Practice Problem 1
sections.rationale: The legacy text teaches that playing in the rain caused Boima's cold. Colds are caused by viruses, so the example now teaches that 'after' is not 'because'. Reviewer to confirm.

sections.heading: 11. Guided Practice Problem 2
sections.rationale: Repeats Problem 3's pattern and showed its answers inline; Problem 3 is kept instead.

sections.heading: 12. Guided Practice Problem 3
sections.rationale: Boimah's stall reused as a reading text with items.

sections.heading: 13. Independent Practice — Tier 1 Foundational
sections.rationale: Zoe and Kollie problems reused; answers were printed next to the problems and are now feedback after a choice.

sections.heading: 14. Independent Practice — Tier 2 Standard
sections.rationale: Answers were printed with the problems; the time-management item is covered by the retention task.

sections.heading: 15. Independent Practice — Tier 3 Advanced
sections.rationale: The St. Paul River clean-up is reused without a signal word, to practise implicit causes; the river is no longer named, to avoid an unverified ecological claim.

sections.heading: 16. Group Discussion and Cross-Curricular Connection
sections.rationale: A useful optional class discussion; it does not produce individual evidence.

sections.heading: 17. Assessment, Exit Ticket, and Lesson Summary
sections.rationale: The personal-reflection exit questions cannot show the objective; replaced by unseen-text written tasks with rubrics.
